papers.title: Composition Theorem for Randomized Query Complexity
papers.abstract: For bounded-error randomized query complexity, we resolve the composition conjecture up to logarithmic factors. The general upper bound $R(f\circ g) = O\!\left(R(f)R(g)\log(R(f)+1)\right)$ was already known. Although Meiburg recently disproved constant-factor multiplicative composition for total Boolean functions, the conjecture allowing polylogarithmic losses remained open. We settle this question by proving that, for all (possibly partial) Boolean functions $f$ and $g$, \[ R(f\circ g) = \Omega\!\left(\frac{R(f)R(g)}{\log(n+1)}\right), \] where $n$ is the input size for $f$.

papers.title: Faster Treasure Hunt via Strongly Universal Exploration with Polylogarithmic Overhead
papers.abstract: We study deterministic exploration and delayed-activation treasure hunt in anonymous undirected port-labeled graphs with incoming-port information. From polynomial-time constructible ordinary universal exploration sequences of length \(O(n^c)\) for a fixed regular degree, we construct a single infinite strongly universal exploration sequence with cover time \(O(n^c\log^2n)\). Summable dyadic insertion schedules yield the sharper bound \(O_\eps(n^c\log n(\log\log n)^{1+\eps})\) for every fixed \(\eps>0\), together with refinements at every fixed iterated-logarithm depth. The proof combines reversible excursions, neutral guards and an arbitrary-window argument that treats both orientations simultaneously. For this recurrence, uniform linear expansion is equivalent to convergence of the normalized period sum. Exact counting identities also permit direct instruction access. With a logspace ordinary generator, table-free enumeration of decreasing scale paths computes instruction \(t\) using \(O(\log(t+2))\) working bits and time polynomial in \(t\). The earlier polynomial-slack bounds follow as corollaries. A local cubic simulation extends the treasure-hunt application to arbitrary-degree graphs, with the \(2m\)-vertex replacement size included explicitly in the bound.

papers.title: Hardness of Approximation for Polynomial Optimization over Sphere for Linear Programming Relaxation Hierarchy
papers.abstract: Semidefinite programming (SDP), particularly the sum-of-squares (SoS) hierarchy, provides $n^{O(q)}$-time approximation and certification algorithms for optimizing degree-$d$ homogeneous polynomials on the unit sphere. For arbitrary inputs, degree-$q$ SoS gives a powered-objective approximation factor $O_d((n/q)^{d/2-1})$ [BGGLT17]. For random order-$d$ tensors, degree-$d$ SoS has an integrality-gap lower bound of $2^{-O(d)}(n/d)^{d/4-1/2}$ relative to the true spherical maximum; lower bounds also extend to growing SoS degree in tensor PCA [BGL17,HKP17]. We establish lower bounds for weaker linear-programming relaxation hierarchies. Our degree-$q$ moment LPs impose the sphere identities and any prescribed, instance-independent family $\mathcal{G}$ of valid polynomial inequalities of degree at most $q$. They include Sherali--Adams-type product hierarchies. For every even $d\ge2$, constant $C>0$, and $q$ satisfying $2d | q$ and $2d\le q\le n$, every such relaxation with at most $n^{Cq}$ tests has instances $P$ satisfying \[ \frac{\mathrm{PowLP}_{q,\mathcal{G}}(P)}{\|P\|_\infty}\ge \frac{c_{d,C}}{\sqrt{q\log n}}\left(\frac nq\right)^{d/2-1/2}.\] Here $\|P\|_\infty$ is the maximum absolute value of the polynomial over the sphere and $\mathrm{PowLP}_{q,\mathcal{G}}(P)$ is the relaxed objective. The exponent $d/2-1/2$ improves the leading dependence on $d$ relative to the $d/4$-type exponents in prior random-tensor SoS lower bounds. Our LP hierarchies impose weaker positivity conditions than semidefinite moment relaxations. It leaves open whether analogous degree dependence can be achieved in lower bounds for SDP hierarchies.

papers.title: Quantum Interactive Proofs of Proximity
papers.abstract: We initiate the systematic study of quantum interactive proofs of proximity (QIPPs). These are quantum interactive proof systems with sublinear communication, where the verifier accepts inputs in a property $\Pi$ and rejects inputs $\varepsilon$-far from $\Pi$, while only querying the input a sublinear number of times. 1. We show that all logspace-uniform $\mathbf{NC}$ properties admit QIPPs with query, communication and time complexity all $\widetilde{O}(n^{2/5})$. This improves on the best known classical total complexity of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt n)$, which is optimal in the worst case for polynomial-time verifiers under the PRG assumption of Kalai and Rothblum (CRYPTO, 2015). This resolves an open question of Dall'Agnol, Gur, Roy Moulik, and Thaler (Quantum, 2022) in the affirmative. 2. Assuming the existence of a post-quantum subexponentially secure PRG computable in logspace-uniform $\mathbf{NC}$, we prove that, for every nondecreasing, logspace-computable query bound $q(n)\le n^{1/2-\Omega(1)}$, there exists a property $\Pi$ in logspace-uniform $\mathbf{NC}$ and a constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that no polynomial-time $\varepsilon$-QIPP for $\Pi$ can achieve query complexity $q(n)$ and communication complexity $c(n)$ satisfying $q(n)+c(n)=o(n^{1/3})$. 3. We establish a bi-directional connection between QIPPs for logspace-uniform $\mathbf{NC}$ and query-model QIPs for parity. A QIP for $k$-bit parity with total complexity $k^{2/3-\Omega(1)}$ yields QIPPs for every logspace-uniform $\mathbf{NC}$ property with total complexity $n^{2/5-\Omega(1)}$. Conversely, achieving total complexity $o(n^{2/5})$ within the standard $\mathsf{PVAL}$-based framework requires improving the known query-communication tradeoff for parity. Additionally, we show that almost every size-$2^{\beta n}$ property ($0<\beta<1$) requires linear total QIPP complexity at constant proximity.

papers.title: Reconfiguration of Time-Bounded Descriptions
papers.abstract: Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity measures a string by the length of its shortest program that prints it within a deadline. An adjunction-universal machine (Bauwens, Kozachinskiy, and Shen, arXiv, 2025) is a Turing machine that simulates every Turing machine $M$ on every input $z$ with polynomial overhead when given a code of $M$, computable from $M$ in polynomial time, followed by $z$ unchanged. Any two adjunction-universal machines give the same measure up to an additive constant and a polynomial change of the deadline. However, this measure records only the shortest program for a string. We study all programs of one length that print a string within one deadline, join two of them when they differ in one bit, and ask when this graph is connected. Fix any adjunction-universal machine. For almost all $m$-bit strings and every deadline beyond some polynomial, the graph is disconnected at program length $m+O(1)$ and has at least $2^{m-O(1)}$ components at length $2m+3$. In contrast, we build an adjunction-universal machine in which every such graph is connected or empty, at every deadline, once the program length reaches a computable threshold that is at most exponential in the length of the string. Exponential thresholds are unavoidable: for every adjunction-universal machine with such thresholds and every large $m$, more than three quarters of the $m$-bit strings need a threshold exponential in $m$. For our machine, above the threshold, every program for the string is within three bit flips of a connected set of fastest programs for the string, along a path inside the graph, at every deadline by which that program halts. For this machine, deciding whether two given programs are connected in this graph is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete when the input is the string, the deadline in unary and the two programs; for each fixed string it takes polynomial time.

papers.title: Deterministic factorization of constant depth circuits from whitebox PIT
papers.abstract: We show that over the field of rational numbers, there is a deterministic algorithm for factorization of constant depth circuits that makes calls to a (whitebox or blackbox) PIT algorithm for such circuits. The time complexity of the algorithm (and hence the number of calls to the PIT oracle) is polynomially bounded in the size and degree of the input circuit. Our reduction to PIT is fairly simple and general and applies as it is to other natural classes of algebraic circuits like formulas and algebraic branching programs. Prior to this work, the known deterministic factorization algorithms for constant depth circuits crucially relied on \emph{blackbox} PIT [Bhattacharjee et al.]. Our main technical ingredient is an efficient, deterministic algorithm that, when given access to sufficiently high degree truncations of \emph{all} the power series roots of a constant depth circuit, uses oracle calls to any (whitebox or blackbox) PIT algorithm for these circuits, and partitions the roots into the sets of conjugates; thereby identifying the irreducible factors. For our proof, we rely on a root recombination criterion using logarithmic derivatives [Sasaki et al., Bostan et al., Lecerf] and show that this criterion can be efficiently and deterministically implemented for power series roots of constant depth circuits using access to any PIT oracle. On the way, we discuss an algorithm that may be of independent interest: it takes as input a matrix whose entries are multivariate constant depth circuits over a field $\mathbb{F}$, requires oracle access to any PIT algorithm for these circuits and outputs a basis for the $\mathbb{F}$-kernel of this matrix in polynomial time.

papers.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
papers.abstract: We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial. The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $\epsilon$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $\epsilon$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/\epsilon$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set.In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(\epsilon)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/\epsilon^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis. On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.

papers.title: Path Isolation and Reachability in Surface-Embedded Graphs with Restricted Cycle and Cut Structure
papers.abstract: We study the reachability problem in directed surface-embedded graphs under two structural restrictions, using isolating weight assignments. First, we consider graphs whose underlying undirected embeddings contain at most polynomially many simple surface non-separating cycles. We develop a polynomially bounded, logspace-computable skew-symmetric edge-weight assignment with nonzero circulation around every simple cycle. This yields an unambiguous logspace (UL) upper bound for directed reachability. The construction also gives an SPL upper bound for bipartite perfect matching in the corresponding undirected graph class. Second, for $g$-genus directed graphs admitting a balanced hierarchical genus decomposition with $O(\log n)$ crossing edges at every partition, we obtain an unambiguous $O(\log g \cdot \log n)$-space bound for reachability. Our approach combines path-isolating weights for lower-genus subgraphs using polynomially bounded FKS hashing refinements at successive merging levels.

papers.title: Hardness of Unique Shortest Vectors and Bounded Distance Decoding
papers.abstract: We prove randomized NP-hardness of the unique shortest vector problem (uSVP) at every constant uniqueness factor greater than one, and of bounded distance decoding (BDD) at every fixed positive fraction less than one half of the minimum distance, in both their threshold decision and search versions. Both results hold in every fixed $\ell_p$ norm with $1\le p<\infty$. Previous Euclidean NP-hardness results for the search versions reached uniqueness factors tending to one and decoding radii greater than the minimum distance divided by $\sqrt2$. For linear codes over every fixed finite field and each fixed ${0<\rho\le1/2}$, the decision version of BDD with radius strictly less than $\rho$ times the minimum distance is equivalent under deterministic polynomial-time reductions to satisfiability for circuits promised to have at most one satisfying input. It is therefore NP-hard under randomized polynomial-time reductions. Earlier hardness for decoding general codes applied beyond half the minimum distance. For every fixed $p>2$ and for $p=\infty$, there is a constant $\epsilon>0$ such that, under randomized polynomial-time reductions, uSVP in the $\ell_p$ norm is NP-hard at uniqueness factor $n^\epsilon$, and BDD in the $\ell_p$ norm is NP-hard at radius $\lambda_1/n^\epsilon$, where $n$ is the lattice rank and $\lambda_1$ is its minimum distance.

papers.title: On Positive Computation
papers.abstract: We introduce new notions of reducibility for monotone classes and show that a monotone version of Circuit Satisfiability and the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem are complete for $mNP$, even under positive reductions (which are not the same as monotone reductions). If this holds for all (monotone) $mNP$-complete problems - that they are also so complete for $mNP$ -, then $P\neq NP$. We introduce positive models of relativized computation and show that the separation $posP\subsetneq mNP$ does not relativize, even when oracles are restricted to monotone sets. Yet, there is a (weak) diagonalization proof that $posP\subsetneq mNP$.

papers.title: Tensor value and the 9/4 bound for matrix multiplication
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent result that the exponent of matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 valid over every field. Our main tool is a fractional symmetrized variant of the tensor value introduced by Coppersmith and Winograd, used in place of spectral points (tensor characters) in the original proof. We prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums, whose summands share one tensor factor and occupy independent subspaces in the other two. Together with the degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof, this inequality yields the bound.

papers.title: Metric Dimension Parameterized by Bag-Connected Treewidth and Bag-Connected Pathwidth
papers.abstract: The metric dimension of a graph is the minimum size of a set of vertices whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices of the graph. We prove that \MetricDimension{} is NP-complete on planar graphs of treewidth and bag-connected treewidth exactly three. The graphs in our construction have no induced cycle longer than four and have (prefix-connected) pathwidth at most four. In particular, the problem admits no XP algorithm parameterized by bag-connected treewidth unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$. This answers questions of Bonnet and Purohit and of Bousquet, Deschamps, and Parreau. We prove that the problem is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by bag-connected pathwidth.

papers.title: A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
papers.abstract: Aaronson and Ambainis conjectured that every bounded polynomial of low degree on the discrete cube has an influential variable. They showed that the conjecture implies that the acceptance probability of every quantum algorithm making $T$ queries can be approximated on most inputs by a classical algorithm making $\mathrm{poly}(T)$ queries. We prove their conjecture: every function $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to[-1,1]$ of degree at most $d\ge1$ has a variable of influence at least $c\,\operatorname{Var}(f)^{5/2}/d^{6}$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. In the original formulation, for polynomials of degree at most $d$ with values in $[0,1]$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ and variance at least $\varepsilon$, this gives a variable of influence at least $(\varepsilon/d)^{7}$. The proof is elementary, with steps inspired by works of others. Thus, as Aaronson and Ambainis anticipated, superpolynomial quantum speedups in the query model require structure, such as a promise on the inputs.

papers.title: Precedence Constraint Scheduling on a Fixed Number of Machines
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic exact algorithm for $P_m\mid\mathrm{prec},p_j=1\mid C_{\max}$ for every fixed $m\ge3$. The algorithm constructs an optimum schedule in $$ O(L)+m^{O(m^2)}\, n^{6m^2+13m+1} \, {\log n} $$ elementary RAM operations, where $n \ge 2$ is the number of jobs and $L$ is the binary input length. Its word size is $O(m^2 \log n)$ bits. An implementation with a fixed number of tapes uses $O(L)+m^{O(m^2)} \, n^{12m^2+26m+2} \, \log^3 n$ steps. For three machines the respective polynomial degrees are $94$ and $188$, apart from the displayed logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Improved Approximation and Hardness Bounds for $\beta$-TSP
papers.abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) asks for a minimum-length Hamiltonian cycle in a complete weighted graph. Its approximability depends on the edge lengths: unrestricted instances admit no constant-factor approximation unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, metric instances admit Christofides' $3/2$-approximation, and fixed-dimensional Euclidean instances admit a PTAS. We study $\beta$-TSP, where the edge lengths satisfy $ \ell_{uw}\leq\beta(\ell_{uv}+\ell_{vw}) \qquad \forall\,u,v,w\in V\ \text{pairwise distinct}, \quad \beta\in\left[\tfrac{1}{2},1\right]. $ The condition arises naturally in various settings, for example, when metric travel times are combined with positive service times at the vertices. The previous best approximation algorithm, due to B\"ockenhauer et al., ranges from $1$ at $\beta=1/2$ to $3/2$ as $\beta$ approaches $1$. We obtain a strictly better guarantee for every $1/2<\beta<1$ by combining two simple constructions whose guarantees counterbalance each other. We also improve the best known approximation hardness bound for every $1/2<\beta<1$.

papers.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
papers.abstract: Dallard, Milani\v{c}, and \v{S}torgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor. We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.

papers.title: A Tight Hierarchy for Chain of Thought
papers.abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for extending the computational capabilities of transformer-based models. A growing body of recent work has begun to uncover the fine-grained computational power of transformers augmented with CoT, as well as their connections to classical complexity theory. In this work, we advance this line of research by establishing the first hierarchy theorem for CoT-based computation. Our main result shows that for any reasonable resource bound $r(n) \geq n$ and any $\varepsilon > 0$, \[ \mathrm{CoT}(r(n)) \subsetneq \mathrm{CoT}(r(n)^{1+\varepsilon}), \] where $\mathrm{CoT}(r(n))$ denotes the class of decision problems solvable by transformers using $O(r(n))$ CoT reasoning steps on inputs of length $n$. Our result shows that increasing the number of CoT reasoning steps provably yields strictly greater computational power, establishing CoT steps as a fundamental resource in transformer-based computation. Unlike classical hierarchy theorems, which are typically proved via diagonalization, our approach leverages known coarse-grained simulations between CoT-augmented transformers and Turing machines in both directions. Building on these connections, we adapt the classical padding technique from complexity theory to this setting to obtain a tight hierarchy. A key technical contribution of our work is the implementation of padding within the transformer-based CoT model.

papers.title: The k-Clique hypothesis is dead, for good
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm that solves the $k$-Clique problem for any large enough $k$ and any $n$-vertex graph in $n^{\left(\frac{\omega}{3}-c\right)k}$ time, where $\omega\geq 2$ is the matrix multiplication exponent and $c>0$ is a positive constant independent of both $\omega$ and $k$. This refutes the long-standing $k$-Clique conjecture, regardless of the value of the matrix multiplication constant, even if $\omega=2$. In fact, our algorithm solves the more general problem of counting weighted $k$-Cliques.

papers.title: Beyond the $n/2$ Threshold: Quantum Query Complexity for Computing Hamming Weight and Symmetric Functions
papers.abstract: The oracle-interrogation algorithm [van Dam, FOCS '98] computes every $n$-bit Boolean function with bounded error using $n/2+O(\sqrt n)$ quantum queries. In contrast, parity can be computed exactly using $\lceil n/2\rceil$ queries, but whether an additive overhead beyond $n/2$ is necessary for a single Boolean output has remained open. In this work, we construct an explicit family of symmetric Boolean functions requiring $n/2+\Omega(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries at a fixed positive constant error. We also give an algorithm that recovers the exact Hamming weight using $n/2+O(n^{1/3})$ quantum queries with bounded error, and therefore computes every symmetric Boolean function within the same query bound. Together, these results determine the optimal additive order for Hamming weight recovery and for the worst case over symmetric Boolean functions at sufficiently small constant error.

papers.title: Optimizing Computational-Statistical Runtime for Wasserstein Distance Estimation
papers.abstract: Squared Wasserstein distance is a frequently used tool to measure discrepancy between probability distributions. This distance is typically computed between empirical measures of size $n$ from two underlying random samples. Unfortunately, even in lower dimensional Euclidean space problems $\left( d \in \{2,3\} \right)$, algorithms for Wasserstein distance computation with approximate or exact precision guarantees scale poorly in the runtime as a function of $n$ and the desired precision. In response, we consider the computational-statistical runtime, where the goal is to estimate from samples the Wasserstein distance between potentially smooth measures up to $\epsilon$-additive error in expectation with respect to the sampling; we allow $O(1)$ computational cost for collecting a sample. Towards this, we develop a Sample-Sketch-Solve paradigm where we introduce a regular cartesian grid sketch of the samples. We show that (especially under $\alpha$-H\"older smooth distributions) this can compress the data without increasing asymptotic error, and also regularizes the structure which enables faster exact algorithms. Ultimately, we approximate $W_2^2(P,Q)$ within $\epsilon$ error in $\epsilon^{-\max(2,\frac{d+1+o(1)}{1+\alpha})}$ time for $0 < \alpha < 1$ H\"older smooth distributions $P,Q$ on $(0,1)^{d}$; an optimal $\Theta(\epsilon^{-2})$ for $\alpha > 1/2$ when $d=2$ and nearly optimal as $\alpha \to 1$ when $d = 3$.

papers.title: A note on a problem in communication complexity
papers.abstract: We study bounded-error randomization and majority operators in structural communication complexity. We give a communication-complexity formulation of Tarui's theorem and identify the bounded-error closure of weakly unbounded-error communication with a distributional perturbation of logarithmic margin complexity. Retaining the Boolean guarantee in Tarui's probabilistic polynomials yields the stronger inclusion $\mathsf{PH}^{\mathrm{cc}} \subseteq \mathsf{ZP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}} \subseteq \mathsf{BP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$. We also define a majority operator satisfying $\mathsf{PP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{cc}} = \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$ and use Sasaki's majority formula to prove that $\mathord{\oplus}\mathsf{P}^{\mathrm{cc}} \subseteq \mathsf{PP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$. For the inner-product function modulo two, both the outer index and each inner protocol have logarithmic cost. Together with Forster's lower bound, this gives an explicit witness to the non-idempotence of the majority operator and to $\mathsf{PP}\mathbin{\cdot} \mathsf{PP}^{\mathrm{cc}} \not\subseteq \mathsf{UPP}^{\mathrm{cc}}$. Both the bounded-error closure and the two-level majority class are contained in $\mathsf{PSPACE}^{\mathrm{cc}}$.

papers.title: Concentration Inequalities for Branching Random Walks with Applications to Phase Transitions in CSPs
papers.abstract: A new framework is developed for studying phase transitions in random CSPs, from which a range of new results follows. Motivated by phase transition problems in CSPs, a more general concentration inequality is proved that retains classical sub-Gaussian tails under a mild global linear-growth condition $|S_n| < Cn$, relaxing the bounded-increment assumption to finite exponential moments and requiring neither independence nor the martingale property. We further extend the concentration inequality to branching random walks (BRW), obtaining the first concentration inequality for BRW. As applications, we derive partial differential equations (PDEs) for the $K$-SAT and $q$-COL backbones, yielding new results, including \textbf{(a)} a resolution of the long-standing open question of where $(2+p)$-SAT transition changes from second to first order; \textbf{(b)} rigorous results for $\alpha_d$ in $K$-SAT, which give new lower bounds on the phase transition for 3-SAT (4.0029 vs. 3.51) and 4-SAT (8.360 vs. 7.91); and \textbf{(c)} the prefactor of the 2-SAT critical window.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Discounted Robust MDPs with $L_p$ Uncertainty Sets
papers.abstract: A basic model in sequential decision making is the Markov decision process (MDP), which is extended to Robust MDPs (RMDPs) by allowing uncertainty in transition probabilities and optimizing against the worst-case transition probabilities from the uncertainty sets. The class of $(s, a)$-rectangular RMDPs with $L_p$ uncertainty sets provides a flexible and expressive model for such problems. We study this class of RMDPs with a discounted-sum cost criterion and a constant discount factor. The existence of an efficient algorithm for this class is a fundamental theoretical question in optimization and sequential decision making. Previous results only establish a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for $L_\infty$ uncertainty sets. In this work, our main results are as follows: (a)~we show that for any compact uncertainty set, the policy iteration algorithm for RMDPs is strongly polynomial with oracle access to solutions of Robust Markov chains (RMCs); (b)~we present strongly polynomial-time bounds on the policy iteration algorithm for RMCs with $L_1$ and $L_\infty$ uncertainty sets; and (c)~we establish hardness results for RMCs with $L_p$ uncertainty sets for integer $p$ satisfying $1<p<\infty$. Finally, motivated by our theoretical bounds, we present experimental results showing how fast policy iteration converges for RMDPs with $L_1$ and $L_\infty$ uncertainty sets.

papers.title: From Block Orthogonality to Decidability in Complex-Weighted Counting CSP
papers.abstract: In a landmark JACM paper recognized with the 2021 G\"odel Prize, Cai and Chen established a complexity dichotomy for counting CSPs over arbitrary finite domains with algebraic complex weights. Their tractability criterion consists of three conditions on the infinite family of functions obtained from CSP instances by summing out some variables: the Block Orthogonality and Type Partition conditions, and a Mal'tsev polymorphism condition on support and row-equivalence relations. They left open whether this criterion is decidable from the finite set of constraint functions. We resolve this question by giving a total exact algorithm for every $q$-element domain ($q\ge 1$), with algebraic weights encoded exactly. We also prove that the Block Orthogonality condition implies the other two conditions, reducing the tractability criterion to a single structural property. We obtain similar decidability and structural results for Lin's tractability criterion for $\#\mathrm{CSP}^{d}$, where each variable occurs a multiple of $d$ times. Our method first shows that every failure of Block Orthogonality can be witnessed by a generated function of arity at most $q^2+1$. At each such arity, we reduce checking infinitely many generated functions to finitely many exact algebraic tests, using tensor products and a pinned extension of Young's all-instance isomorphism theorem. For the structural implication, we use powers of generated functions to control complex cancellation and construct functions whose supports encode row equivalence. These constructions yield the Type Partition and Mal'tsev polymorphism conditions.

papers.title: A Dichotomy for Complex Boolean Holant with Binary Disequality
papers.abstract: We classify Boolean Holant problems with a supplied binary disequality signature and an arbitrary fixed finite set of algebraic complex-valued signatures. Each problem is polynomial-time computable or $\#\mathsf{P}$-hard, and the tractability criterion is decidable. The proof combines arity reduction with the growth of the available binary transfer group and uses stable pairs to recover the structure of higher-arity signatures. We also prove a dichotomy for the disequality-edge model when the signature set contains an endpoint-nondegenerate irreducible eight-vertex signature, resolving the corresponding arity-four cases in the main proof.

papers.title: Bounded Relative Boundary Implies Narrow DNF Approximation
papers.abstract: We prove Friedgut's conjecture (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999)) that every increasing family in the $p$-biased discrete cube with bounded relative boundary can be approximated arbitrarily well by one whose minimal elements have size bounded independently of the dimension and the bias. For $0<p\le 1/2$, every increasing Boolean function with total resampling influence at most $K$ is $\varepsilon$-close under $\mu_p^n$ to a monotone DNF of width $\exp(O((K+1)^2/\varepsilon^2))$, from which the full conjecture follows for all $p\in(0,1)$. We build on Hatami's pseudo-junta theorem (Ann. of Math. 176 (2012)), whose approximator need not be increasing. Our randomized shifts produce an increasing approximator that is measurable with respect to a controlled refinement of Hatami's adaptive partition. Retaining only short positive certificates yields the desired narrow DNF.

papers.title: A Full Complexity Dichotomy for Complex-Valued Boolean Holant Problems
papers.abstract: A Boolean Holant problem evaluates a graph partition function specified by local signatures at its vertices. We prove a complexity dichotomy for arbitrary finite sets of algebraic complex-valued signatures on general graphs: an explicit, decidable criterion characterizes the polynomial-time cases, and every remaining case is $\#\mathsf{P}$-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. The proof resolves the all-even case by constructing signatures with nonzero endpoints and all remaining support on the central layer, then classifying them according to half their arity. Binary transfer groups and matching-product reconstruction provide the main tools in the small- and large-height cases, respectively.

papers.title: High Precision Multiplicative-Error Approximation of $\#$SAC$^1$ Functions in Logspace Uniform AC$^1$
papers.abstract: We show that approximations of $\#\mathsf{SAC}^1$ functions (i.e. functions computed by logspace-uniform polynomial-size positive semi-unbounded arithmetic circuits of depth $O(\log n)$) can be computed in logspace uniform $\mathsf{AC}^1$ (denoted as $\mathsf{L}\text{-}\mathsf{AC}^1$) with multiplicative error $2^{-\operatorname{poly}\log n}$.Previously, approximations of $\#\mathsf{SAC}^1$ functions were known to be in logspace-uniform $\mathsf{TC}^1$ via exact computation given by Allender, Jiao, Mahajan, and Vinay (TCS'98). A main corollary of our result is that the following models beyond $\mathsf{BPL}$ are computable by $\mathsf{L}\text{-}\mathsf{AC}^1$ with multiplicative error $2^{-\operatorname{poly}\log n}$: - Probabilistic Auxiliary Push-down Machines (Probabilistic $\mathsf{AuxPDM}$s), which are polynomial time logspace Turing Machines (TMs) with an auxiliary stack having unbounded size and a read-once random tape; - Read-$k$ Probabilistic TMs with polynomial time and logarithmic space, where $k$ is a constant and Read-$k$ means the random tape is two-way accessible and each cell can be visited for at most $k$ times. Notice that this is a direct generalization and improvement for $\mathsf{BPL}\subseteq\mathsf{L}\text{-}\mathsf{AC}^1$ of Cheng and Wang (CCC'24), and the approximation error is improved from additive reverse polynomial to multiplicative reverse quasi-polynomial. $\mathsf{AuxPDM}$ was introduced by Cook (JACM'71) and its probabilistic version was first studied by Macarie and Ogihara (TCS'98). Read-$k$ Probabilistic logspace TMs was studied by Impagliazzo, Nisan, Wigderson (STOC'94) where a pseudorandom generator for this model was given. We mention that multiplicative error approximations are stronger than additive error approximations in the sense that they can even be used to decide non-deterministic computations.

papers.title: Two-colour crossing minimization in complete geometric graphs is NP-hard
papers.abstract: Given a fixed straight-line drawing of a complete graph, we seek a two-colouring of its edges that minimizes monochromatic crossing pairs. We prove that the threshold decision problem is NP-complete, even for points in general position with integer coordinates. Thus exact minimization is NP-hard, resolving the complexity question posed at the Crossing Number Workshop in 2019. We reduce from MaxCut on permutation graphs by representing source vertices with classes of geometric edges, whose crossings encode source adjacencies. The target complete graph also contains every other edge between its points, and their freely chosen colours can affect the encoded cost. To control these interactions, we construct a large comparison grid with two stable colour phases and use program points to turn this reference into colour preferences on other edges. The optimum differs from a computable baseline plus the amplified minimum number of uncut source edges by an error small enough to distinguish consecutive source values. The reduction is deterministic, with polynomially many points and polynomial coordinate bit length.

papers.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
papers.abstract: We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler-extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997). Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $\delta\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $$ m+O_\alpha(\log(D/\delta))\text{ random bits and } O_\alpha\!\left(\varepsilon^{-2-\alpha}\log^{1+\alpha}(D/\delta)\right)\text{ samples}, $$ for any constant $\alpha>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1+\alpha} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_\alpha(a+\log(1/\eta))$ and seed length at most $(1+\alpha)\log a+(2+\alpha)\log(1/\eta)+O_\alpha(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $\eta$. We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-\Omega(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/\eta))$ and output length $\Omega(n)$, improving previous constructions.
